name: Clear + Brilliant

lead: Clear + Brilliant is a gentle fractional laser from Solta Medical, often nicknamed a baby Fraxel. People use it as an entry-level refresh for tone, texture and early signs of aging, with minimal downtime.

Its 1440 nm handpiece and 1927 nm Perméa handpiece create tiny zones of thermal injury while leaving surrounding skin intact, prompting collagen remodeling and skin turnover for a brighter tone and finer texture. Published human data come from small trials covering photoaging, periorbital rejuvenation and melasma in groups of 14 to 40 people.

paras: Clinics perform it in a series of sessions and sometimes repeat it as maintenance, positioned as preventive skin upkeep. Results are described as lasting months.
Mild redness is reported to resolve quickly. As a laser procedure it carries general fractional-laser risks.

angle.text: Clear + Brilliant is a mild fractional laser people use as a starter or maintenance treatment for tone and texture, with minimal downtime. It creates tiny treated zones so the surface renews and collagen remodels. Small trials in photoaging, periorbital rejuvenation and melasma support its use.

lead: Clear + Brilliant is a non-ablative fractional laser made by Solta Medical and offered in dermatology and aesthetic clinics to even out skin tone, refine texture and soften the early signs of aging. People book a series of short sessions to look fresher and smoother, with brighter, more even-looking skin, less visible pores and softer fine lines, and the skin is typically pink for only hours to a day afterwards [1][2]. It is often called a "baby Fraxel" or "starter laser" because it belongs to the same fractional family as the stronger Fraxel devices [1][3].

The device scatters thousands of microscopic columns of thermal injury across the skin while leaving the tissue between them intact and the outer surface in place. The body repairs those zones and turns over skin cells, a process that proponents link with improved radiance and texture [1][2]. The original handpiece uses a 1440 nm diode laser, the Perméa handpiece uses 1927 nm, and the Touch model delivers both in one session [1].

The published literature consists mainly of small prospective studies, case series and registered trials in photoaging, periorbital rejuvenation, melasma and pigmentation, with group sizes from 4 to 40 participants [4][5][6][7][8][9][10][11]. Claims of high satisfaction and millions of treatments worldwide come largely from the manufacturer and from encyclopedic summaries [1][2].
infobox: Both wavelengths in one system, US launch March 2021 [1]
Four to six sessions, per manufacturer [2]
Described as little to none; redness 12 to 24 hours [2]
Marketed for Fitzpatrick types I to VI [1]

paras: Clear + Brilliant is a console with handpieces that deliver laser light through disposable contact tips. A computer-controlled scanning motor places a grid of tiny treatment zones across the face, neck, chest, hands or other areas [1]. The manufacturer describes patented optical tracking that keeps the handpiece in contact with the skin for even coverage [2].

The brand is aimed at people who want to improve how their skin looks before significant aging has set in, and at those who want to maintain results from other treatments [1][2]. The manufacturer's FAQ says the treatment may complement fillers, Thermage or botulinum toxin at the treating physician's discretion [2].

Skin laser resurfacing is generally divided into ablative lasers, which vaporise tissue and create wounds (for example CO2 at 10,600 nm and Er:YAG at 2940 nm), non-ablative lasers that leave the surface intact, and fractional devices that treat a pattern of points [12]. Clear + Brilliant is a non-ablative fractional laser and is described as milder, with shorter recovery, than Fraxel Restore (1550 nm), Fraxel Restore Dual (adds a 1927 nm thulium laser) or the ablative Fraxel Repair (CO2) [1][3].

The 1440 nm handpiece is the original Clear + Brilliant wavelength and is used for general texture, tone and early aging concerns [1]. The 1927 nm Perméa handpiece acts more superficially and has been studied for pigmentation, periorbital skin and melasma [1][6][7][8][10]. Clinics sometimes combine the laser with other energy devices; a 2025 study paired 1440 and 1927 nm treatment with monopolar radiofrequency [9].

The concept behind these devices, fractional photothermolysis, was licensed from the Wellman Center for Photomedicine at Massachusetts General Hospital. R. Rox Anderson is named as inventor of the technology behind Fraxel, which Reliant Technologies commercialised from 2004 [3]. Solta Medical later grouped Fraxel and Clear + Brilliant in its portfolio [1].

According to Grokipedia, Clear + Brilliant received FDA 510(k) clearance in May 2011, the Perméa handpiece was added in 2012, and the dual-wavelength Clear + Brilliant Touch launched in the US in March 2021 [1]. That page is AI-generated and its dates were not independently verified.

Fractional photothermolysis delivers energy as a pattern of microscopic thermal zones in the epidermis and dermis. Skin between the zones is untouched, so healing proceeds from the surrounding tissue, and because the surface is not removed the barrier is largely preserved [1][2].

Proponents describe the wound-healing response as stimulating fibroblasts, new collagen and elastin remodelling, plus faster epidermal turnover, which they connect with smoother texture and brighter tone [1]. The manufacturer says the system creates hundreds of thousands of microscopic treatment zones that replace damaged skin [2].

Manufacturer information lists a 30 to 45 minute appointment, with about 15 to 20 minutes of active treatment. A topical numbing cream is optional [2][1]. Visible improvements are reported by the manufacturer after four to six treatments, spaced weeks apart (some protocols use two to six weeks), with optional maintenance afterwards; some people report softer, brighter skin within a week or two [2][1]. Results are said to last for months depending on age, skin condition and sun protection [2].
Practice varies by clinic. Some protocols combine the two wavelengths in one visit, use 1927 nm on its own for pigment or the eye area, or add topical agents such as cysteamine for melasma [5][7][6].

A prospective study of 28 adults (89 percent women, mean age 40) given four full-face treatments one month apart with both wavelengths reported significant improvement from baseline in all photodamage measures at 1 and 3 months; about 96 percent rated their overall appearance as improved, and no serious adverse events were recorded [8]. The study had no control arm.

A prospective single-arm study of 20 women with mild to moderate facial laxity and photoaging combined 1440 and 1927 nm laser with monopolar radiofrequency. At 6 months, scores on the Skin Laxity Grading Scale and Glogau photoaging classification improved; blinded reviewers correctly identified 67 percent of post-treatment photographs, 77 percent of participants were responders, and no serious adverse events occurred [9].

For periorbital skin, a 2025 open-label trial randomised 20 participants to 1927 nm treatment at 2-week or 4-week intervals. Both groups improved in skin lightness and pigmentation scores; the 4-week group also improved pore index and wrinkle scores. Transient tenderness, redness, swelling and scaling mostly resolved within 7 days [10]. A registered 1927 nm periorbital study (n=20, started 2023) is also on record [6]. A 2026 case series of four women with Fitzpatrick skin types III to IV reported progressive improvement in infraorbital pigmentation, brightness and texture without post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation [11].

For melasma, a retrospective review of 11 patients treated with a pulsed dye laser plus 1927 nm laser found more than 50 percent improvement in 6 of 11 (54 percent), with no rebound melasma or adverse events noted [13]. A registered trial combined 1927 nm laser with topical cysteamine for facial melasma (n=20, started 2022) [7].

Registered studies also include a combination versus laser-only photoaging trial (n=14, started 2018) [4] and a study of the Touch 1440/1927 nm device in photoaging (n=28, started 2021) [5]. A 2025 literature review of the 1440/1927 nm system described skin reactions as mild to moderate and self-limited, with high patient satisfaction and no serious events among reported studies [14]. For non-laser comparison, a registered phase 2/3 study of a skin care regimen for photoaging signs (n=40, started 2024) is also on record [15]. The Grokipedia summary notes that most of its sources are manufacturer or clinic materials and that it gives no effect sizes [1].

Common effects listed by the manufacturer are redness and swelling that usually settle within 12 to 24 hours, plus itching, dryness, sensitivity, discomfort and, rarely, pinpoint bleeding [2]. Studies report erythema, edema, crusting, tenderness, scaling and heat sensation as expected, short-lived reactions [8][10][14].

Grokipedia lists rarer complications as pigmentation changes, infection, scarring and prolonged redness, and lists contraindications including active skin conditions, keloid tendency, immune-compromising conditions, recent oral steroids, isotretinoin use, recent cosmetic procedures and recent botulinum toxin or filler; it advises against use in pregnancy [1]. The manufacturer's safety information mentions retinoid use within two weeks, and botulinum toxin or filler within two weeks, as possible exclusions [2]. Fractional lasers in general have been associated with herpes simplex and acne outbreaks in a study of 961 treatments, and anecdotal online accounts describe pigmentation changes and scarring after fractional treatments [3][12].
The system is marketed for Fitzpatrick skin types I to VI, and authors of the 2025 literature review cite its use in skin of color [1][14].

The treatment is a common offering in dermatology and medspa practices, marketed for glow, pore appearance and maintenance, and the brand claims millions of procedures worldwide [1][2]. Wavelength options and handpiece names are part of how clinics advertise it.

Looksmaxxing forums frame skin quality as an important part of facial attractiveness. A widely read looksmax.org guide argues that clear skin creates an impression of health, youth and hygiene even with average facial structure, and lists basic skincare, targeted treatments and clinic procedures as routes to it [16].

lore.intro: Online, Clear + Brilliant is mentioned as a gentle clinic option within broader discussion of skin quality, acne scarring and pigmentation, alongside skincare, retinoids and isotretinoin [16].

claims.claim: It is a "starter laser" with almost no downtime
A course of four to six sessions visibly improves tone and texture
The 1927 nm handpiece can improve pigmentation and melasma
Clear skin is a high-impact appearance upgrade, and procedures can help get there

timeline.event: Reliant Technologies launches the Fraxel fractional laser line based on technology licensed from the Wellman Center [3].
Clear + Brilliant receives FDA 510(k) clearance, per Grokipedia [1].
Retrospective study of pulsed dye plus 1927 nm laser for melasma published in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine [13].
Registered trial of combination versus laser-only treatment for photoaging begins [4].
Dual-wavelength Clear + Brilliant Touch launched in the US (March), per Grokipedia; Touch photoaging study registered [1][5].
Studies of 1440/1927 nm laser for photoaged skin, with radiofrequency, and for periorbital rejuvenation published; a literature review of its safety follows [8][9][10][14].
